name: Katana Kitten
take: A Japanese-American cocktail bar that behaves like a party: highballs and martinis upstairs, a louder room downstairs, and nobody sipping quietly.
theCatch: Walk-in only and loud by 7; come at opening on weekends or plan to stand.
notes: Two floors on Hudson at Charles; open till 2am Mon-Sat, midnight Sunday. Cocktails roughly $13-22 with a snack menu of nori fries, wings and sandwiches. A regular on World's 50 Best lists, which brings a line on weekend nights.

name: Angel's Share
take: Basement bar with the strictest house rules in the neighborhood, and cocktails precise enough that you stop minding them.
theCatch: Walk-in only, parties of four max, no standing, closed Sunday and Monday; get there near 5pm.
notes: Moved from the East Village to a Grove Street townhouse basement in 2020. Opens 5pm Tue-Sat; no reservations, no standing, no groups over four, no splitting parties. Japanese snacks alongside the drinks; jazzy, low-volume room.

name: Sip & Guzzle
take: Two bars stacked in one Cornelia Street townhouse: a quiet, serious cocktail room below and a rowdier pub upstairs, so you can pick your night.
theCatch: Book Sip 10 days out at midnight; Guzzle takes walk-ins and keeps a late menu after 10:30.
notes: Opened 2024 from Shingo Gokan of Angel's Share. Guzzle (upstairs, classic cocktails, pub energy) runs 4pm-1am Sun-Tue and till 2am Wed-Sat; Sip (downstairs, bespoke cocktails) opens at 5pm. Reservations via SevenRooms 10 days ahead; walk-ins nightly, late-night menu after 10:30pm is walk-in only.

name: Donna
take: A worker-owned tropical cocktail bar on Cornelia where you can hear each other, with a real happy hour and Latin snacks that count as dinner.
theCatch: Happy hour runs 5-7 on weekdays and fills fast; Sunday it closes at 9.
notes: Reopened in 2023 as a worker-owned cooperative after the Williamsburg original closed. Mon-Thu 5pm-midnight, Fri-Sat till 1am, Sun 3-9pm; happy hour Mon-Fri 5-7pm with discounted cocktails. Pan-Latin snacks; Resy reservations available but not required.

name: St. Jardim
take: A West 10th wine bar the size of a studio apartment: low-intervention bottles, a record player, and nobody rushing you out.
theCatch: Only a handful of tables, so book on Resy or come on a weeknight.
notes: Café from 7:30am most days, switches to wine bar and dinner at 5pm; cavatelli, hanger steak, cheese plates. Around six tables plus bar seats, sidewalk tables in warm weather, magazines and records. Resy.

name: Le Dive West Village
take: The West Village outpost of the Canal Street spritz-and-tartare scene: a big sidewalk patio, a bar-tabac interior, and everyone you follow on Instagram.
theCatch: Walk-in only; the patio is gone by 5pm on a nice day, so come early or take the inside.
notes: Second location of the Dimes Square wine bar, at 7th Ave S and W 11th. Spritzes, martinis, pét-nat and steak tartare; large sidewalk seating plus a Parisian-styled room inside. No reservations; outdoor tables are the draw and go early.

name: Blind Tiger
take: The beer bar other beer bars measure themselves against: 28 taps, a few casks, a wood-and-brick corner room, and three-deep at the bar by 8.
theCatch: Open till 4am but the room is tight; weekday afternoons are when you get a stool and a chat.
notes: Bleecker at Jones; daily 11:30am-4am. 28 rotating drafts plus three casks and 50-odd bottles and cans, with a bar-food menu. Fills up nights and weekends; regulars go in the afternoon to talk beer with the bartenders.

name: WXOU Radio Bar
take: A cash-only Hudson Street dive with a rock jukebox, baseball junk on the walls, and bartenders who've decided you're a regular by your second beer.
theCatch: Cash only, and the room is one narrow bar; bring a few people, not a party.
notes: 558 Hudson between Perry and W 11th; Mon-Fri 3pm-4am, weekends from 1pm. Cash only. Named for the antique clock on the wall; jukebox skews classic rock; bottles, a few drafts and well drinks, no food.

name: Art Bar
take: Front room for the after-work crowd, back room with couches and a fireplace for the rest of the night, and a kitchen that's still open at 2.
theCatch: $5 drafts and wells 4-7 daily; claim a couch in the back before 9 on weekends.
notes: 8th Ave between Jane and Horatio; daily 4pm-4am, kitchen till 2am (3am Fri-Sat). Happy hour 4-7pm every day with $5 draft, well, house wine and sparkling. Booths up front, overstuffed couches and a working fireplace in back, rotating local art, digital jukebox. A neighborhood fixture for 30-plus years.

name: Corner Bistro
take: A 1961 corner tavern where the burger is the whole menu: cheap beer, a booth if you're early, and open till 4 on weekends.
theCatch: Cash only (there's an ATM); the burger line moves fastest weekday afternoons.
notes: W 4th at Jane under the orange neon; Sun-Wed 10am-2am, Thu-Sat 10am-4am. Cash only, walk-ins only. Same family since the 1960s; a brief 2024 closure was for new flooring, not a shutdown. An East Village outpost opened on Ave A. Booths fill at dinner; afternoons are easy.

name: Julius'
take: The city's oldest gay bar is still a low-key neighborhood tavern: cheap drinks, cash only, and a grill burger better than it needs to be.
theCatch: Cash only; on weekends the grill runs late and the burger line is real.
notes: W 10th at Waverly. A bar since the 1860s and a gay bar since mid-century; site of the 1966 Sip-In. Mon-Thu 4pm-2am, Fri 4pm-4am, Sat noon-4am, Sun noon-2am. Cash only. Grill does burgers, hot dogs, grilled cheese, onion rings.

name: Marie's Crisis
take: A basement piano bar where the whole room sings show tunes at full volume; nobody's watching you, and by 10:30 you can't get through the door.
theCatch: Cash only, tip the pianist, and keep your phone down; piano starts 5:30 and it's standing room by 10.
notes: Grove at 7th Ave S, downstairs; open from 4pm daily, music from 5:30pm until close (around 4am). Cash only, $1 coat check, a drink minimum; filming on phones is discouraged. Show-tune sing-along every night; quiet early, heaving by 10:30, waits of 15-25 minutes are normal.

name: Cubbyhole
take: A tiny lesbian bar with a ceiling full of decorations, a jukebox, and a crowd that has been the neighborhood's living room since 1994.
theCatch: Cash only and packed shoulder-to-shoulder Friday and Saturday; weeknights you can actually get to the bar.
notes: 281 W 12th at W 4th; Mon-Thu 4pm-2am, Fri 4pm-4am, Sat 2pm-4am, Sun 2pm-2am. Happy hour 4-7pm, weekly events (Michelada Mondays, craft nights), games on TV with $5 beer specials. One very small room; cash only per Infatuation.

name: Smalls
take: A basement jazz room where the music is the point: sets from 6pm, a jam that runs toward 4am, and a bar that doesn't pretend otherwise.
theCatch: Tickets are per set and sold online; standing room fills, so pick your set and show up early.
notes: Basement at 183 W 10th near 7th Ave S. Sets nightly around 6, 7:30, 9 and 10:30pm; after-hours jam roughly 11:30pm to 4am. Ticketed per set via smallslive.com, also livestreamed. Sister room Mezzrow is across the street.

name: Cellar Dog
take: Pool, ping-pong, shuffleboard and a live jazz band in a giant basement under Christopher Street: the rare bar where ten people have something to do.
theCatch: $5-10 cover after 6, tables by the hour, and almost no food; eat first or bring it in.
notes: The old Fat Cat space, reopened as Cellar Dog. Mon-Thu 4pm-1am, Fri 4pm-4am, Sat 2pm-4am, Sun 2pm-1am. Cover $5 Sun-Thu and $10 Fri-Sat after 6pm; jazz from 7pm nightly; nine pool tables, six ping-pong, six shuffleboard, foosball and board games at $8-9 an hour. Drinks $5-13; kettle chips and small charcuterie only, outside food allowed. 21+ after 6.

name: Wogies
take: A basement Philly bar on Greenwich Ave: cheesesteaks on house-baked rolls, wings, every Eagles game with the sound up, and a regular crowd that knows the bartenders' names.
theCatch: Eagles Sundays are standing room only; any other night you'll get a booth and a $6 well drink at happy hour.
notes: 39 Greenwich Ave, below street level; Sun-Thu 11:30am-2am, Fri-Sat till 3am. Philadelphia-sports bar: cheesesteaks, wings, house-baked bread, $6 well drinks at happy hour, booths and tables plus TVs. Packed for Eagles games, quiet otherwise. Open 20-plus years.

name: Down the Hatch
take: A subterranean sports dive on W 4th with wings, half-price drinks till 7, and a back room for the ten of you who couldn't decide.
theCatch: Half off everything weekdays 2-7; it's an NYU-adjacent basement, so expect loud and young on weekends.
notes: 179 W 4th between 6th Ave and Jones; Mon-Fri 2pm-4am, Sat-Sun noon-4am. Half-off all drinks Mon-Fri 2-7pm; wings are the order, weekend brunch till 4pm. Semi-private back room with high-tops and exposed brick for groups. Around 35 years in the neighborhood.

name: The Stonewall Inn
take: The bar the riots are named for is still a working two-floor gay bar: a long bar downstairs, drag and karaoke upstairs, dance parties Friday and Saturday.
theCatch: Bring a physical ID; most nights are no cover, and the second floor is where the show is.
notes: 53 Christopher St; Mon-Fri 2pm-4am, Sat-Sun 1pm-4am. Two floors: piano bar Tue-Wed, pool and karaoke Thursday, karaoke Friday, drag shows Sat-Sun, dance parties Fri-Sat from around 10pm; most weekly events have no cover. 21+ with physical ID. The national monument is across the street, so tourists early, locals late.

name: Minetta Tavern
take: The 1937 tavern Keith McNally turned into a red-banquette steakhouse: the burger is the reason people fight for the table, the bar is the reason to stay.
theCatch: Reservations go fast on Resy; try the bar for a walk-in seat, and the late supper menu runs 11 to midnight.
notes: 113 MacDougal at Minetta Lane; dinner nightly 5-11pm, supper 11pm-midnight, lunch Wed-Fri, brunch weekends. Resy. Dark wood, checkerboard floor, red banquettes, caricature-covered walls; known for the Black Label burger, steaks and the chocolate soufflé.

name: Buvette
take: A tiny French bar on Grove where the tables touch, the wine is by the glass, and a croque madame at 11pm feels like the right decision.
theCatch: Open 8am to midnight; there's a wait most nights, so put your name down and get a drink nearby.
notes: 42 Grove at Bleecker; open daily 8am-midnight with food served all day. Very small room with bar seats, a few sidewalk tables and a back garden; largely walk-in, and reviewers report lines at brunch and dinner. French small plates, croque madame, steak tartare, coq au vin; wine and cocktails.

name: Cowgirl
take: Frozen margaritas, Frito pie and longhorn skulls on Hudson Street since 1989: the birthday-dinner place that doesn't mind eight of you and a cake.
theCatch: All-day happy hour on frozen and rocks margaritas; call ahead for a big table on weekends.
notes: 519 Hudson at W 10th; Mon-Thu and Sun 10am-11pm, Fri-Sat till midnight. Tex-Mex and smoked meats, frozen and rocks margaritas at happy-hour prices all day, frozen espresso martinis. Dining room, bar, lounge and a private room, plus an outdoor patio; reservations by phone or email.

name: Boucherie West Village
take: A 320-seat brasserie in an old theater on 7th Ave South: steak frites, a proper bar, and enough room that a last-minute six isn't a crisis.
theCatch: Loud on weekend nights and books up; kitchen runs to midnight, which makes it the late dinner option.
notes: 99 7th Ave S between Grove and Barrow, in the former Circle Repertory Theater. Mon-Fri 11am-midnight, Sat-Sun from 10am. 320 seats across a high-ceilinged main room, butcher-counter seats, a second-floor gallery and an outdoor café; dry-aged steaks, French onion soup, escargot, crème brûlée. OpenTable; weekends book up.

name: Don Angie
take: Italian-American with the volume turned up: the pinwheel lasagna everyone photographs, a room that feels like a party, and a walk-in bar that opens before the tables.
theCatch: Tables release on OpenTable seven days out and go instantly; the bar opens at 4:30 for walk-ins.
notes: 103 Greenwich Ave at W 12th; bar from 4:30pm (3:30 Fri-Sun), dinner from 5pm (4pm Fri-Sun), last seating 10:30pm, lunch Fri-Sun. From Angie Rito and Scott Tacinelli; lasagna for two is the signature. Reservations on OpenTable released a week ahead; the bar is the walk-in route.

name: Emmett's on Grove
take: Tavern-style thin-crust pizza and a proper bar on Grove Street, open till 1 on weekends: the low-stakes dinner before Marie's Crisis or Angel's Share up the block.
theCatch: Walk-ins depend on the room; put your name in on Resy and have a drink up the block while you wait.
notes: 39 Grove between Bleecker and Bedford; Mon-Tue 5-11pm, Wed-Thu till midnight, Fri noon-1am, Sat brunch then 4pm-1am, Sun till 11pm. Tavern-style thin-crust pizza with a wine and cocktail list; Resy plus walk-ins. Sibling of the deep-dish Emmett's on MacDougal.

name: The Red Lion
take: Bleecker Street's live-music bar with a floor people actually dance on: a cover band every night, a crowd that sings along, and last call at 4.
theCatch: There's a cover once the band starts on weekend nights, and by midnight it's a wall of NYU and bachelorettes. That's the point, not a warning.
notes: Bleecker at Thompson. Bands nightly from around 9-10pm; rock and pop covers, occasionally originals. Open till 4am. Sports on the TVs earlier in the evening. Two bars, a small stage, standing room that turns into a dance floor.

name: The Bitter End
take: The oldest rock club in the city, still booking three or four acts a night under the brick wall everybody's been photographed in front of.
theCatch: It's a music venue with a bar, not a bar with music: a cover at the door, a two-drink minimum, and the set list decides your night.
notes: Open since 1961. Nightly bills of several acts, mostly singer-songwriter and rock; tickets or cover $10-20 plus a two-drink minimum at the tables. Shows start around 7-8pm and run late on weekends.

name: Groove
take: A funk and soul band seven nights a week in a room the size of a living room, and by the second set nobody is sitting.
theCatch: No cover most nights but a two-drink minimum; the band starts around 9 and it's shoulder to shoulder by 11 on weekends.
notes: MacDougal between Bleecker and W 3rd. Live R&B, funk and soul nightly; two-drink minimum, small cover some weekend nights. Open till roughly 3am on weekends.

name: Café Wha?
take: The basement where Dylan and Hendrix played before anyone knew their names, now a house band that plays every hit you own and a room that dances in the aisles.
theCatch: Book a table ahead; there's a cover and a reservation system, and the house band's set is the reason you came, so don't show up at 1am expecting a bar.
notes: Basement club at MacDougal and Minetta Lane, open since 1959. Reservations with a cover charge, tables with a food menu; the Café Wha? house band plays rock, soul and pop covers most nights, with themed nights (Brazilian, funk) on others.

name: Terra Blues
take: Up a flight of stairs on Bleecker, a blues bar that does it properly: an acoustic set early, an electric band late, and people who came to listen.
theCatch: A cover kicks in after the early set and the good seats go before the band plugs in; get there for the acoustic show and stay.
notes: Second floor, Bleecker between Thompson and LaGuardia. Blues nightly: solo acoustic around 7pm, full band around 10pm; cover in the $10-15 range once the band's on. Open till around 3am on weekends.

name: Off The Wagon
take: An NYU bar and proud of it: pitcher deals, pong tables in the back, a DJ on weekends and a crowd that thinks 1am is early.
theCatch: If you're over 26 you'll feel it. Come for the happy-hour prices and the game, not for a conversation.
notes: MacDougal just north of Bleecker. Long happy hours with pitcher and pint deals, beer pong and pool in the back, TVs everywhere, a DJ late on Fridays and Saturdays; open till 4am.

name: White Horse Tavern
take: The 1880 corner tavern on Hudson: wood, tile, sidewalk tables, a pint of something honest, and a hundred and forty years of people arguing at the bar.
theCatch: It's a landmark, so the sidewalk fills with tourists on a nice afternoon and the inside is small. Go in, not out, if you want the real thing.
notes: Hudson at W 11th. Opened 1880; the Dylan Thomas story is on the wall. Sidewalk seating in season; a proper bar inside; pub food. Busy on sunny weekend afternoons.

name: Bayard's Ale House
take: A neighborhood ale house on Hudson with the game on, a long tap list, and a burger that's a reason on its own. Nobody's performing anything.
theCatch: Big games pack it wall to wall; on a quiet night it's just a good pub. Know which one you're walking into.
notes: Hudson at Charles. Taps, TVs, burgers; a neighborhood pub that fills for big games. Two blocks from the White Horse.
